title: Probing the digital exposome: associations of social media use patterns with youth mental health
authors: Pagliaccio D, Tran KT, Visoki E, DiDomenico GE, Auerbach RP, Barzilay R

primary_models.name: Exposome-wide association study (separate linear mixed-effects models) of BPM Total Problems T-score on each digital/social media exposure, adjusted for age, sex, race, and Hispanic ethnicity
primary_models.location_in_paper: Methods, Statistical analysis (ExWAS steps a-f, p. 3); Results 'ExWAS (training sample)' pp. 3-4; Fig. 2A (Manhattan plot) and Fig. 2B (forest plot of coefficients with 95% CI), p. 4; full coefficients in Supplementary Table S1 (not in PDF). Interpreted in Discussion pp. 6-7.
primary_models.design: Cross-sectional. Both exposures and outcome come from the ABCD 2-year follow-up visit (2019-2020, mean age about 12). One observation per child. Each of 41 retained digital exposures was entered as the sole exposure in its own LME model; there is no time structure and no exposure-by-time interaction. The ABCD sample was first split into matched training and testing subsamples (ABCD Reproducible Matched Samples); the ExWAS was run in the training subsample and its coefficients were used as weights to build the digital exposomic risk score applied in the testing subsample.
primary_models.sample: ABCD Data Release 4.0, participants who completed the 2-year follow-up including screentime and social media assessment (N = 10,147). ExWAS run in the training subsample, n = 5082 (testing subsample n = 5065). Training subsample (Table 1, p. 4): age M = 12.01 (SD 0.66); 2446 (48.13%) female; SGM identity 406 (7.99%); race White 3901 (76.76%), Black 985 (19.38%), American Indian/Alaska Native 169 (3.33%), Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander 34 (0.67%), Asian 313 (6.16%), other 317 (6.24%), mixed 608 (11.96%); Hispanic ethnicity 1014 (19.95%); non-social screentime 24.88 (SD 13.97) hours/week. Missing exposure data were imputed with missForest separately within each subsample; outcome values were not imputed. The per-model analytic N for the ExWAS is not reported in the main text.
primary_models.iv: Each of 41 digital and social media exposure variables, one per model, drawn from the ABCD Cyber Bullying Questionnaire and the Youth and Parent Screen Time Surveys (youth and parent report). Of 52 candidate variables, 7 were dropped for <1% endorsement and 4 for collinearity (|r| > 0.9); extreme values on continuous variables (e.g., number of followers) were removed. Exposures span five domains: screentime (minutes/hours per day by weekend/weekday), parental monitoring of social media (e.g., parent suspects secret accounts), apps used (yes/no per platform, platform-specific screentime, most-used app), overuse/addictive patterns of use (e.g., 'I use social media apps so much that it has had a bad effect on my schoolwork or job'), and peer interaction (e.g., connectedness via phone). Exact coding and units per variable are in Supplementary Table S1 and the Supplement, not the main text. Of the 35 FDR-significant exposures, 31 are phone/SM-specific and are extracted here; cyberbullying and three video-game screentime items are not. No descriptive statistics for the exposures are given in the main text, apart from 48% reporting a public account and 16% reporting TikTok as most-used app.
primary_models.dv: Brief Problem Monitor (BPM) Total Problems T-score, youth self-report, age- and sex-normed; reflects internalizing, externalizing, and attentional problems. Measured at the 2-year follow-up. No descriptive statistics for BPM T-scores reported in the main text.

covariates.name: Race
covariates.detail: Two binary indicators: identifying as Black; identifying as White

primary_models.equation: BPM_T[i] = b0 + b1*exposure_k[i] + b2*age + b3*sex + b4*Black + b5*White + b6*Hispanic + u_site + u_family(site) + e[i], estimated separately for each exposure k = 1..41
primary_models.estimation: R, lme4::lmer linear mixed-effects models with random intercepts for family nested within study site. Missing exposure data imputed with missForest (random forest) within each subsample. Collinear exposures (Pearson r > 0.9) removed with caret::findCorrelation. FDR correction across the 41 comparisons; exposures with FDR-corrected p < 0.05 and coefficient > 0 treated as risk factors, < 0 as protective; 35 of 41 survived. Sensitivity: ExWAS rerun with list-wise deletion instead of imputation yielded 31 significant variables (Table S1, not in PDF); per-variable sensitivity estimates not in main text. No interaction tests at the ExWAS level. No survey weights reported.

d_transformation.native_metric: B (unstandardized LME coefficient, BPM T-score points per unit of exposure)
d_transformation.conversion_formula: Binary exposures: d = B / SD_DV (adjusted mean difference over SD 10). Continuous exposures: beta_std = B * SD_IV / SD_DV; d = 2 * beta_std / sqrt(1 - beta_std^2) (Borenstein et al. 2009 eq 7.1).
d_transformation.contrast_type: Per one unit of each exposure as coded in Table S1: yes vs no for binary items (e.g., public vs private account), per unit of time or count for continuous items. Units are not given in the main text.
d_transformation.notes: SD_DV = 10 by construction for BPM T-scores (normed), but BPM T-scores are floor-truncated in community samples so the observed SD may differ; the paper reports no BPM descriptives. SD_IV is not reported for any exposure in the main text, and exposure units/coding are only in the Supplement. Only one qualifying coefficient is printed as a number in the main text (public social media account, B = 2.13, Discussion p. 6, no CI); this is binary, so d is computable with SD_DV = 10. All other 30 qualifying coefficients and all CIs are in Fig. 2B (graphic only) and Supplementary Table S1, which is not in the PDF. With Table S1, the binary items become convertible; continuous items still need SD_IV. [complete-stage 2026-10-01] Re-read entire PDF (10 pp.) and searched docs/pdfs for a '_supplement' file for this DOI (none). No additional per-exposure estimates, CIs, SEs, exact p-values, t-statistics, or exposure SDs are printed; Fig. 2B is an unlabelled forest plot. Model iv_type set to continuous with per-estimate iv_type='binary' overrides for public account, secret accounts, parent-suspects-secret-account, and top-app TikTok (prevalences reported in Discussion p.6). SD_DV = 10 (T-score convention) retained. [complete-stage 2026-10-01] Supplement (docx) is now bundled and was read in full. Its Table S1 is a variable list, not a coefficient table: no per-exposure B/CI/SE/p are printed anywhere, so 30 of 31 cells remain without a value and the one printed B (public account 2.13) has no CI input. Table S1 does give coding/units: '[n] Screentime <App>' items (#12-22) are actually number of accounts on that app (0-10), not time; #2,#3,#5,#6,#7,#8 are hours; #28-33 are 1-6 frequency scales; #34-36 are 1-4 nights/week; #39 is 1-7 agreement; #40-41 counts (>5000 removed). The public/private item (#38) is listed as '1=Public; 0=Private, Reverse coded for analysis'. The 6 non-significant exposures are #10 parent follows child on SM, #17 Pinterest accounts, #23-26 most-used app Instagram/Snapchat/YouTube/Multiplayer chat (not bolded in Table S1); no estimates printed for these either. No exposure SDs printed (sd_iv unavailable).

extraction_flags:
1. Missing supplement. The PDF is the 10-page main article only. All per-exposure ExWAS coefficients and CIs are in Supplementary Table S1, which was not available. In the main text they appear only as a forest plot (Fig. 2B). The only qualifying number printed in the text is public (vs private) social media account, B = 2.13 (Discussion p. 6), with no CI. The other 30 qualifying cells are B = null on purpose: I did not read values off the plot. To fill them, get Table S1 from the online supplement at 10.1038/s44277-024-00006-9.

2. Sample label conflict. The Methods and Results headings say the ExWAS ran in the training subsample (n = 5082). The Fig. 2 caption says "testing subsample". I followed the Methods; please check.

3. Units and coding of exposures are not given in the main text. SD_IV and per-model N are not reported. SD_DV is set to 10 because BPM scores are normed T-scores, but BPM T-scores are floor-truncated, so the observed SD may differ.

4. Six non-significant exposures (Table S1 numbers 10, 17, 23, 24, 25, 26) are not named in the main text. Some are probably phone/SM null results and should be added once Table S1 is available.

5. Eligibility calls a coder should check:
- Included: "Night chatroom use" (platform not specified), "Connectedness via phone", "Parent suspects secret account" (parent report) and "Follower/Following count".
- Excluded as gaming: "Screentime Video Games [20]", although Fig. 2A puts it in the App-type domain, so it may be app-based.
- Excluded: cyberbullying, per FT-IC2 clarification 3.
- Excluded: the headline exposomic risk score (Table 2, and the suicide-attempt ORs in Table S3). It is a weighted composite that includes cyberbullying and video-game items, so it fails FT-IC2 Step 2.

6. Spot-checked against the page images: Table 1 training demographics, Table 2 Model-4 (1.78, 1.58-1.98, t = 17.41, n = 4004), the text values 2.13 and 3.57, and the suicide ORs 1.76 [1.39-2.23] and 2.76 [1.88-4.05].
